checked_source_locators.source_assumptions: PartialOrder; weak closure is equivalent to strict closure via equality case.
checked_source_locators.book_difference_and_obligation: Book lower closure is strict q<a; this matches after checking equality separately. Nonempty/proper/no-max are additional conditions, not consequences of lower closure.

checked_source_locators.source_assumptions: Set complement of a lower set is an upper set, for the existing ambient order.
checked_source_locators.book_difference_and_obligation: Complement alone is not a negative cut. Reflection turns upper into lower but does not remove a possible maximum.
Applicable to established Q, not to not-yet-constructed cut arithmetic.

checked_source_locators.source_assumptions: Given a<b, midpoint strictly between; no completeness.
checked_source_locators.book_difference_and_obligation: For q<−r choose (q−r)/2, keeping the same complement witness; this proves no maximum for the strict negative cut.

checked_source_locators.source_assumptions: Field/order structure; library rational proof uses rational ceiling in an intermediary step.
checked_source_locators.book_difference_and_obligation: Book already has QG1 explicit rational-record bound; use it on (b0−a0)/δ to get a natural exit bound, without real Archimedean property, floor or cut arithmetic.

checked_source_locators.source_assumptions: CommGroup, PartialOrder, IsOrderedMonoid; multiplicative text marked to_additive.
checked_source_locators.book_difference_and_obligation: Read source annotations only, no Lean elaboration/compilation. The additive specialization may be applied to Q whose additive laws are proved. It does not assume or prove that newly constructed cuts form a group.

checked_source_locators.source_assumptions: Pointwise operation on arbitrary subsets; lower closure when the indicated factor is lower, in the prior ordered-group context.
checked_source_locators.book_difference_and_obligation: Book proves exact-sum lower closure using a′=p−b; it must separately prove nonempty, proper and no maximum. Do not treat library lower closure as cut closure.

checked_source_locators.source_assumptions: Reflection/inverse changes upper to lower and lower to upper in an ordered group.
checked_source_locators.book_difference_and_obligation: Source guarantees only lower closure of reflected complement. Book N(A)={q:∃r∉A,q<−r} has an additional strict rounding step. For A=i(0), raw reflected complement is {q≤0} and fails no-maximum.

checked_source_locators.actual_locator: LowerSet One / Mul / coe_mul, to_additive annotations
checked_source_locators.source_assumptions: Bundled lower sets use image2 of ambient operation; all lower sets allowed.
checked_source_locators.book_difference_and_obligation: Image2 corresponds to exact rational sum witnesses, but neither the restricted type nor its zero is the book type. Exact and strict sum witness equivalence must be proved from no-max/downward closure.

checked_source_locators.actual_locator: LowerSet One defined by Iic 1, to_additive
checked_source_locators.source_assumptions: Additive translation of this definition gives the CLOSED lower segment Iic 0.
checked_source_locators.book_difference_and_obligation: Book 0_R=i(0)=Iio(0) excludes rational zero. Cannot cite library zero/unit proof as the book proof; use an internal larger a and z=q−a<0 in the reverse inclusion.

checked_source_locators.source_assumptions: Commutative monoid of all lower sets, with closed principal unit. No cut inverse construction here.
checked_source_locators.book_difference_and_obligation: Only a comparison for inherited associativity/commutativity. Book nested witness proofs establish these on restricted cuts; DA1 is still required for inverse reverse inclusion. Arbitrary lower sets do not all have additive inverses.

checked_source_locators.source_assumptions: add_assoc and add_comm are fields required of structures.
checked_source_locators.book_difference_and_obligation: They name obligations, not automatic theorems of the new cut operation. Prove by two-direction witness regrouping using only old Q laws.

checked_source_locators.source_assumptions: Existing SubNegMonoid plus a neg_add_cancel proof; subtraction convention discussed.
checked_source_locators.book_difference_and_obligation: Book must prove A⊕N(A)=0_R in both directions before using inverse uniqueness, double negation or cancellation.
After the laws are proved, the name describes the concrete structure. It is not a prior abstract axiom or a claim of ordered field / multiplication.

checked_source_locators.source_assumptions: Existing complete R, lower rational subset bounded above, sup_R A not a member.
checked_source_locators.book_difference_and_obligation: This source characterizes cuts after R already exists. Do not obtain small rational boundary gaps from an assumed real supremum/density. Book uses Q grid and natural least index instead.

checked_source_locators.source_assumptions: Real Archimedean property is proved using sup_R N; Q density in R is subsequently derived.
checked_source_locators.book_difference_and_obligation: This route would assume the target ambient real structure. Book needs Q-only Archimedean bound and least natural index, and does not call cut-supremum either.

checked_source_locators.actual_locator: Part I §VI Operations with Real Numbers
checked_source_locators.source_assumptions: Two-sided historical cuts; C1 membership uses c≤a1+b1; endpoint may be assigned to the first side.
checked_source_locators.book_difference_and_obligation: Not literally the modern strict-cut definition. For BOOK cuts, exact, ≤-witness and <-witness versions can be connected by lower closure and no maximum; the historical endpoint convention cannot simply be dropped.

checked_source_locators.actual_locator: §VI rational addition compatibility and halving positive gap
checked_source_locators.source_assumptions: Rational endpoints and two-sided cuts; splits positive p into two halves to produce members.
checked_source_locators.book_difference_and_obligation: Book independently uses h=(r+s−q)/2 and exact witnesses r−h,s−h; prove both inclusions for strict principal lower sets.

checked_source_locators.source_assumptions: Author says other operations may likewise be defined and discusses scope, without supplying this book strict-negation/grid inverse proof.
checked_source_locators.book_difference_and_obligation: Do not cite this paragraph as a complete proof of strict negative cuts, ε-grid lemma, inverse law, order translation, or subsequent multiplication/root existence.

independent_derivation_observations.conclusion: Nonempty natural set has unique least element, proved by strong induction and classical contradiction; not a newly adopted axiom.

independent_derivation_observations.source_status: independent derivation from actual QG1, ord-a07 and rational arithmetic; no exact external theorem claimed
independent_derivation_observations.claim: 0<v−u<epsilon with one interior and one exterior rational

independent_derivation_observations.source_status: no inspected external source gives the complete exact N(A) construction plus endpoint check and inverse proof
independent_derivation_observations.claim: Book must carry the full four-condition and epsilon-grid proof; related library reflection proves only closure direction

independent_derivation_observations.source_status: independent construction proof; abstract source declarations only describe required laws

book_proof_obligations.obligation: Separate each internal a from external b by rational trichotomy and lower closure. For epsilon>0 set delta=epsilon/2; choose a0∈A,b0∉A and QG1 positive natural N with eta(N)delta>b0−a0. E={n:a0+eta(n)delta∉A} is nonempty, excludes 0. Use ord-a07 least m; m=k+1 gives k∉E. Then u in, v out, v−u=delta strictly between 0 and epsilon. No cut arithmetic, cut supremum, real density or simultaneous choices.

Well-ordering yields a least member of a specified nonempty natural set under classical logic. An arbitrary cut supplies no decidable membership predicate, so no general executable first-exit search, computed real boundary, or terminating cut API is inferred. A rational principal-cut example may have an independent decision procedure.

A⊕B={q:∃a∈A,b∈B,q=a+b}. Internal a0+b0 gives nonempty; external r+s is outside because all a+b<r+s; p<q=a+b uses a′=p−b<a; increasing a gives no maximum. Only after four conditions declare R×R→R, with exterior equality giving a unique output subset.

For book cuts, q=a+b can be strengthened to q<a1+b by increasing a. Conversely q<a+b gives exact q=(q−b)+b with q−b<a. A weak q≤a+b version also needs equality or lower closure. Historical cuts that admit endpoint maxima are not silently equivalent to this restricted convention.

N(A)={q:∃r∉A,q<−r}. External r0 gives −r0−1 inside; internal a0 makes −a0 outside; same external witness gives lower closure; midpoint (q−r)/2 gives no maximum. Do not identify it with raw −A or raw reflection of complement. For i(0), raw reflected complement {q≤0} has maximum 0.
i(r)⊕i(s)=i(r+s): forward sum of strict inequalities; backward q<r+s, h=(r+s−q)/2>0, a=r−h,b=s−h, a+b=q. Covers negative and zero endpoints with exact rational arithmetic.
N(i(r))=i(−r): external t means t≥r so q<−t≤−r; converse use external t=r. Principal compatibility does not prove all-cut laws since nonprincipal cuts exist.
Exchange witnesses; expand both nested sum memberships before using rational associativity. A⊕i(0)⊆A follows from z<0. Reverse uses q<a∈A then z=q−a<0; rational zero is NOT in i(0).

Forward q=a+c with c<−r, r∉A, a<r gives q<a−r<0. Reverse any x<0: DA1 with epsilon=−x yields v−u<−x, hence c=x−u<−v, so c∈N(A) and x=u+c. A nonstrict gap may yield equality and fail the negative-cut witness; strictness is essential.

After both inverse inclusions, use already established association, commutation and unit to prove inverse uniqueness. Then N(N(A))=A, cancellation, and group terminology. Do not assume any of these in DA1 or in inverse existence.

Weak monotonicity follows from member inclusion. Reflection requires adding N(C) after inverse law. Strict preservation follows from weak preservation plus equality cancellation; strict reflection similarly excludes equality. Translation T_C has two-sided inverse T_N(C), a function on established cut set R.

A⊆B gives r∉B⇒r∉A, hence N(B)⊆N(A). Reflection uses double negation only after DG2. Prove inverse of sum by actual parenthesized rearrangement and uniqueness. Define A⊖B=A⊕N(B), then solve A⊕X=B uniquely and derive order-by-difference from translation.

Use existing Q and cut-set P(Q) background, products and conditional subsets. No new unrestricted object collection or choice axiom. All witnesses are selected for one given input/claim; no global choice function. No real multiplication, inverse/division, roots, limits, or complete ordered-field claim.

adopted_vs_proved.adopted: Only prior explicit classical logic and set background including batch21 P(Q), products and conditional subsets; no new Archimedean/completeness or group axiom for cuts.
adopted_vs_proved.proved_before_use: QG1 and ord-a07 must be linked to their actual files; book proves cut closure, unit, inverse and order laws before using them.
not_adopted: Existing complete real field or rational density in it
mathlib full lower-set closed zero Iic(0)
Historical two-sided endpoint identification without translation
Decidable membership or a first-exit algorithm for arbitrary cuts
Choice functions, cut multiplication, real square roots or limits

critical_mismatches: Book strict i(0)=Iio(0) versus library all-LowerSet additive zero Iic(0).
Historical C1 uses weak sum witness and allows endpoint allocation; book exact/strict sum equivalence uses no maximum.
Pointwise reflection of complement can include a largest endpoint; the book strict q<−r definition removes it.
Abstract group laws and already-built R sources cannot be premises of the same cut construction.
